user.title: Energy sensors
user.description: Select energy (kWh) sensors. Production and storage: as many as you like. Feed-in: exactly one. Each of them gets a filtered copy that ignores short drops to 0; use it as source for utility_meter.

data.storage_combined_energy_sensors: Combined storage sensors (in and out, energy, optional)
data.invert_storage_combined: Combined storage sensors: positive = into storage (default: positive = from storage)

data_description.reset_confirm_minutes: Minutes a lower value must persist before it counts as a real reset. Shorter drops are ignored.

power.title: Power sensors
power.description:
Select power (W) sensors, same layout as the previous step.

Note: if your system has several strings (e.g. different orientations such as east/west), select the individual string sensors here. Do not pick a total sensor that sums strings with different orientations, otherwise they cannot be told apart. Sensors that only report one direction (production, feed-in, into storage, from storage) are counted with their positive values; a sensor with a sign (e.g. a battery that charges and discharges) belongs in the combined storage field.

data.storage_combined_power_sensors: Combined storage sensors (in and out, power, optional)
data.invert_storage_combined_power: Combined storage sensors: positive = into storage (default: positive = from storage)
data.invert_feed_in_power: Feed-in sensor reports feed-in as negative values (invert sign; default: positive = feed-in)
data.abs_storage_power: Storage in/out sensors report negative values (use the magnitude; default: only positive values count)

data_description.production_power_sensors: Select one sensor per string, not a total across different orientations.

forecast.title: Forecast
forecast.description: Optional forecast energy (kWh) sensors, e.g. from Forecast.Solar or Solcast. Several sensors per field are possible (e.g. one per string).

grid.title: Grid, consumption and prices
grid.description: Optional. Grid import and house consumption enable autarky and exact self-consumption; the battery level, irradiance and prices enable the battery curve, the performance ratio and the savings. If your feed-in power sensor also reports grid import as positive values (see the option in the power step), the import is derived from it automatically.

data.price_import: Grid import price per kWh (sensor or input_number, optional)
data.price_feed_in: Feed-in tariff per kWh (sensor or input_number, optional)

data_description.grid_import_energy_sensors: Energy bought from the grid (kWh). Several meters are summed.
data_description.grid_import_power_sensors: Power drawn from the grid (W), only needed if there is no energy sensor.
data_description.house_energy_sensors: Total consumption of the house (kWh) including everything behind the meter, such as wallbox, heat pump and the like. Use the same scope as the grid import so that autarky and direct consumption add up. If the wallbox is measured separately and not included here, add its sensor as well (several sensors are summed).
data_description.house_power_sensors: Same as the energy field, as power (W). Used for the live curves.
data_description.battery_soc_sensor: Charge level of the battery in %. Only used for the battery curve and the min–max tile.
data_description.irradiance_sensor: Solar irradiance in W/m² from a pyranometer or a weather station (device class irradiance). Used for the performance ratio on the Analysis tab: the yield is compared with what the irradiance should have produced, which separates weather from plant problems. It needs the peak power of the strings (Settings tab). Not the same as a forecast sensor.
data_description.price_import: Current electricity price in €/kWh, used for the savings. A fixed price can be entered under Settings → Plant instead.
data_description.price_feed_in: Feed-in tariff in €/kWh, used for the feed-in revenue.

abort.already_configured: PV Assistant is already set up.
